chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Norman Granz at Normandie Hall and Nat Cole's crushed Studebaker
summary: Callender says Billy Berg's gave Granz the idea for concerts, recalls Sunday sessions at Normandie Hall and Nat Cole giving him a ride.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: We used to broadcast every night. But these jam sessions naturally weren't broadcasted. And that's where Norman Granz first came in the picture. I think Norman was still going to school. He used to come in his tennis shoes. And I think this gave Norman the idea for the Jazz concerts. Because we used to do...Sunday afternoons we used to... There was a place on Normandie and Jefferson, Normandie Hall, and we used to do sessions there. I remember one day... Nat used to pick me up sometimes. He had an, I'd say, old Studebaker...naturally, it wasn't old then, but a tree had just fallen in on it when Nat came by to pick me up, and it had crushed the side in. I remember having to stick my bass through the window and hold it that way. This was before Nat became... Well, he had his trio, but he wasn't, you know, the millionaire Nat King Cole. He was just ordinary Nat King Cole, the piano player, at that point.
What year would that have been?
